record.context_brief: Extremal non-negative rank of the average mixing matrix
record.original_question: For the average mixing matrix Mc of a graph, determine exactly when its non-negative rank is equal to n, the number of vertices. Here the non-negative rank of a non-negative n x n matrix M is the least integer k such that M can be written as a sum of k rank-1 matrices with non-negative entries.

evidence.quote: The non-negative rank of a non-negative n×n matrix M is the least number k, such that there are k matrices {Mr}kr=1 of rank 1 with non-negative entries, such that M = Pkr=1 Mr.
4.2 Open Problem. When is the non-negative rank of Mc is equal to n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite simple graph on n vertices with adjacency matrix A. Write the spectral decomposition A = sum_{r=1}^{d} lambda_r E_r, where lambda_1, ..., lambda_d are the distinct eigenvalues of A and E_r is the orthogonal projection onto the lambda_r-eigenspace. The continuous-time quantum walk on G is given by the unitary U(t) = exp(itA), and the mixing matrix at time t is the doubly stochastic matrix M(t) defined entrywise by M(t)_{u,v} = |U(t)_{u,v}|^2, equivalently M(t) = U(t) circ U(-t), where "circ" denotes the entrywise (Hadamard, Schur) product. The average mixing matrix of G is

   Mc = lim_{T -> infty} (1/T) integral_0^T M(t) dt = sum_{r=1}^{d} E_r circ E_r,

an n x n symmetric doubly stochastic matrix with non-negative entries.

For a non-negative n x n matrix M, define its non-negative rank rank_+(M) as the least integer k for which there exist rank-1 n x n matrices M_1, ..., M_k with non-negative entries such that M = M_1 + ... + M_k.

Problem. Characterize exactly the finite simple graphs G on n vertices for which rank_+(Mc) = n.

artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns characterizing graphs whose average mixing matrix has non-negative rank equal to the number of vertices. Literature on the average mixing matrix (Coutinho–Godsil–Guo–Zhan; Godsil–Guo–Sinkovic and follow-ups) addresses ordinary rank and structure but does not record a known characterization of when its non-negative rank attains n; no resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: A New Perspective on the Average Mixing Matrix
status_evidence.snippet: Defines and studies the average mixing matrix of a graph and its rank.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference for the average mixing matrix; treats rank rather than non-negative rank.

status_evidence.title: Average mixing matrix of trees
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the (ordinary) rank of the average mixing matrix for trees.
status_evidence.claim: No characterization of non-negative rank equal to n is established.

status_evidence.title: Nonnegative rank (linear algebra) — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The nonnegative rank of a nonnegative matrix is the least k such that the matrix is a sum of k nonnegative rank-1 matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Standard definition of non-negative rank used in the problem.
